name: Liu Hsün’s wife
bio: Liu Hsün’s wife lived in the third century AD. After she had been married to General Liu Hsün for a long while he sent her back to her home, because he had fallen in love with a girl of the Ssu-ma family, and she is credited with the poem on the curtain of the wedding bed.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: The Curtain of the Wedding Bed
poems.author: Liu Hsün’s wife
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
Flap, flap, you curtain in front of our bed!
I hung you there to screen us from the light of day.
I brought you with me when I left my father’s house;
Now I am taking you back with me again.
I will fold you up and lay you flat in your box.
Curtain--shall I ever take you out again?
